To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electric charge and magnetic flux are topological charges, that they are related to each other, that they are quantized and that they are fractionalized.

the angular momentum of charged fields, in 2+3 dimensional abelian gauge theory, is not quantized and is not related to the spin of the field, but is related to the magnetic flux carried by the field.

(i) the angular momentum of charged sectors of 3D gauge theories is fractional; (ii) the angular momentum is quantized in units of 2π/3, and (iii) the angular momentum depends on the electric charge and the magnetic flux.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions. What is the physical interpretation of the non-vanishing monodromies of the charged fields? How does this affect the angular momentum of the charged fields?
the following questions.
the construction and analysis of the physical charged fields of 2+3 dimensional gauge theories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the physical sectors of 2 + 1 dimensional gauge theories, electric and magnetic charges are associated with angular momentum.
in the physical charged sectors the spin of the fields is fractional and that the spin of the physical charged fields is related to their electric charge and magnetic flux.
the angular momentum operator of the theory is not well defined, in the sense that its action is not well defined on the Hilbert space of the theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the physical states of 2+ 1 dimensional gauge theories have non-trivial topological properties, which can be interpreted in terms of the non-Abelian structure of their gauge group, or, alternatively, in terms of the anyon statistics of the physical charged fields.
the physical charged sectors are described in terms of anyons.
the angular momentum of charged fields is not a well defined concept in 2+3 dimensional abelian gauge theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the angular momentum of charged fields cannot be defined in the usual sense.
the monodromy of the fields is a consequence of their non-vanishing angular momentum, and that the fractional spin is the angular momentum of the fields modulo 2π.
the angular momentum of the physical charged fields is a topological charge.
